context_label: Ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer
title: Bevacizumab every two weeks with chemotherapy for recurrent ovarian cancer
schedule_label: Bevacizumab every 14 days alongside weekly paclitaxel, weekly topotecan or pegylated liposomal doxorubicin. Your other medicine has its own appointment dates.
schedule_summary: Bevacizumab every 14 days alongside weekly paclitaxel, weekly topotecan or pegylated liposomal doxorubicin. Your other medicine has its own appointment dates.
purpose: Bevacizumab is given with chemotherapy to help control ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer that has returned and is resistant to platinum. Your team chooses one partner medicine.
indication_text: 00212b covers platinum-resistant recurrence after no more than two prior chemotherapy regimens and no prior bevacizumab or other VEGF or VEGF-receptor inhibitor.
administration_text: Bevacizumab every 14 days alongside weekly paclitaxel, weekly topotecan or pegylated liposomal doxorubicin. Your other medicine has its own appointment dates.
monitoring_summary: Full blood count, kidney and liver function. Blood counts, kidney and liver tests, urine protein, and blood pressure before and after treatment. The team checks your INR weekly until stable, then before each cycle. Symptoms, examination and scans according to your treatment plan.
review_status: Independent oncology, pharmacy and patient review pending.

agents.name: Bevacizumab
agents.explanation: Binds VEGF, a signal that promotes blood-vessel growth. Blocking VEGF can reduce the blood supply that supports tumour growth; it also affects normal blood vessels and wound healing.
agents.mechanism: Blocks the VEGF blood-vessel growth signal
visual: Less VEGF signalling supports tumour blood vessels
risks: Raised blood pressure and protein in the urine
Bleeding, blood clots and problems with wound healing
Rare bowel perforation, abnormal internal connections called fistulae, or serious wound infection
Rare severe headache, confusion, seizures or vision changes associated with a brain syndrome
Infusion reactions; fatigue and other effects may be increased by the chemotherapy partner
agents.watch: Report bleeding, severe pain, neurological symptoms or wound problems promptly, and attend blood-pressure and urine checks.
consent_risks: Severe headache, confusion, seizures or a change in vision need urgent help.
Attend blood-pressure checks; chest pain, breathlessness or a swollen painful leg need urgent help.
Urine checks look for protein. Report new swelling, foamy urine or reduced urine.
Sudden severe abdominal pain needs urgent assessment.
Report bleeding or wounds that are painful, red, spreading or slow to heal.
A new swollen painful leg or sudden breathlessness needs urgent help.

common_effects.title: Blood pressure and urine protein
common_effects.text: Blood pressure can rise and protein can leak into urine without causing symptoms. Attend the scheduled checks.

common_effects.title: Nosebleeds and healing
common_effects.text: Tell the team about repeated nosebleeds, new bruising or a wound that is slow to heal.

phases.label: With weekly paclitaxel
phases.detail: Bevacizumab and paclitaxel are both due on days 1 and 15 of the 28-day partner schedule. Paclitaxel also has separate weekly visits.

phases.label: With weekly topotecan
phases.detail: Bevacizumab is due every two weeks. Use the weekly topotecan calendar for additional appointments.

phases.label: With liposomal doxorubicin
phases.detail: Both medicines are given on day 1 of the partner cycle. Bevacizumab is given alone on day 15.

support.title: Between visits
support.text: Call now for new severe abdominal pain, heavy bleeding, severe headache or a change in vision. Call 112 or 999 for sudden chest pain, severe breathlessness, seizure or stroke symptoms. With chemotherapy, fever, chills or suddenly feeling unwell also need urgent assessment.

evidence.title: AURELIA
evidence.interpretation: Across the three chemotherapy choices, median time before progression was 6.7 months with bevacizumab and 3.4 months with chemotherapy alone.
evidence.limitations: These are pooled results. The study did not compare the three chemotherapy partners against each other or establish an overall survival advantage.

agents.name: Bevacizumab
agents.explanation: It reduces signals that help tumours form blood vessels. This can also affect blood pressure, kidneys and wound healing.
agents.mechanism: It reduces signals that help tumours form blood vessels. This can also affect blood pressure, kidneys and wound healing.
visual: It reduces signals that help tumours form blood vessels. This can also affect blood pressure, kidneys and wound healing.
agents.watch: Call urgently for severe abdominal pain, significant bleeding, a new severe headache or sudden weakness.

agents.name: Paclitaxel
agents.explanation: It disrupts cell division. Hair follicles, blood cells and nerves can also be affected.
agents.mechanism: It disrupts cell division. Hair follicles, blood cells and nerves can also be affected.
agents.watch: Report numbness and tell the nurse immediately if you flush or wheeze during treatment.
